overrides.FiniteJet.GraphKoszul.koszulGraph_restri:
Let `E` be a complete nonarchimedean normed commutative ring whose norm unit ball is noetherian, and suppose that `E` has a topologically nilpotent unit which scales the norm multiplicatively. Put `T_E = E⟨T₁,…,T_m⟩` and `r_i = gT_i-f_i`, where `g,f₁,…,f_m` generate the unit ideal of `E`. Then, for every `q ≥ 0`, `im(d_{q+2,E}) = ker(d_{q+1,E})`. Thus every positive-degree Koszul cycle is a boundary.

In Lean, `P E m` is the ring denoted `T_E` in the paper. The theorem is obtained by transporting polynomial Koszul exactness along the flat map `E[T₁,…,T_m] → T_E`.
overrides.FiniteJet.KoszulFree.koszulDifferential_:
Give `∧^q T_E^m` the finite-product topology in the standard exterior basis. For every `q ≥ 0`, the Koszul differential `d_{q+1,E}: ∧^{q+1}T_E^m → ∧^qT_E^m` is continuous.

Lean proves this over any topological ring, since each coordinate is a finite sum of continuous multiplication maps.
overrides.FiniteJet.GraphKoszul.koszulDifferential:
For every `q ≥ 0`, the Koszul differential `d_{q+1,E}: ∧^{q+1}T_E^m → ∧^qT_E^m` is strict onto its image.

In the Gauss-norm/unit-ball case formalised in Lean, this follows from norm-controlled lifts from the image.
overrides.FiniteJet.GraphKoszul.isClosed_range_kos:
For every `q ≥ 0`, `im(d_{q+1,E})` is closed in `∧^qT_E^m`; when `q = 0`, this says that `I_E = (r₁,…,r_m)` is closed in `T_E`.

Lean uses positive-degree exactness and continuity when `q > 0`, and the noetherian closed-ideal theorem when `q = 0`.
overrides.FiniteJet.GraphKoszul.pow_smul_graphIdea:
There is an integer `h_E ≥ 0` such that `ϖ^{h_E}(I_E ∩ T_{E,0}) ⊆ d_{1,E}(T_{E,0}^m)`.

Lean interprets the two lattices as the Gauss-norm and sup-norm unit balls. The result is proved for any finite sequence `r_i` by scaling a norm-controlled lift for `d_{1,E}`.
overrides.FiniteJet.GraphKoszul.pow_smul_ker_d1_in:
There is an integer `z_E ≥ 0` such that `ϖ^{z_E}(ker(d_{1,E}) ∩ T_{E,0}^m) ⊆ d_{2,E}(∧²T_{E,0}^m)`.

Lean uses the standard finite-free coordinate model of `∧²T_E^m`, whose unit ball is `∧²T_{E,0}^m`, and obtains the exponent by scaling a norm-controlled lift for `d_{2,E}`.
overrides.FiniteJetOver.StrictLoc.locRhoC_isOpenMa: For every rational datum, the induced map `C_α → D_α` is open. Lean first proves that the coefficientwise map `T_C→T_D` is open using its norm-preserving section, and then passes openness through the quotient maps. Together with the separately proved continuity and surjectivity, this gives the strict surjection in Proposition 5.3.
overrides.FiniteJetOver.chartDatum_isRational: The datum `(W;ϖ)` defines the rational domain `{|W| ≤ |ϖ|}` used in Section 4.
overrides.FiniteJetOver.chartEquiv_continuous: The ring equivalence identifying the rational chart with `K⟨X,Q⟩/(Q²)` is continuous.
overrides.FiniteJetOver.chartEquiv_symm_continuous: The inverse of the ring equivalence identifying the rational chart with `K⟨X,Q⟩/(Q²)` is continuous. Together with `chartEquiv_continuous`, this makes the equivalence a homeomorphism.
overrides.FiniteJetOver.locRhoC_continuous: For every rational datum, the induced map `C_α → D_α` is continuous.
overrides.FiniteJetOver.presheafValueMapB_restrict: The coefficient map from `A` to `B` commutes with restriction between rational domains. This is the `B`-part of the refinement compatibility in Proposition 5.3.
overrides.FiniteJetOver.presheafValueMapC_restrict: The coefficient map from `A` to `C` commutes with restriction between rational domains. This is the `C`-part of the refinement compatibility in Proposition 5.3.
overrides.ValuationSpectrum.IsSheafy: Let `(A,A⁺)` be a complete nonarchimedean Huber pair. For every finite rational cover of a rational domain, restriction to the covering pieces is required to be a topological embedding, and every compatible family is required to glue. In the complete Tate setting this is the rational-basis form of the topological sheaf condition used in the paper.
overrides.ValuationSpectrum.IsLimitSheaf: For every open `V ⊆ Spa(A,A⁺)` and every open cover `V = ⋃ᵢ Uᵢ`, sections are separated, compatible families glue, and the restriction map `𝒪(V) → ∏ᵢ 𝒪(Uᵢ)` is a topological embedding. This is the all-open topological sheaf condition used in the paper.
overrides.ValuationSpectrum.isSheafy_iff_isLimitSh: For a complete Tate pair, the finite rational-cover condition `IsSheafy A` is equivalent to the all-open condition `IsLimitSheaf A`.
overrides.ValuationSpectrum.IsSheafOfTopologicalRi: For every topological commutative ring `T`, the presheaf `V ↦ Hom_cont(T,𝒪(V))` is a sheaf of sets. This is Wedhorn’s representable formulation of a sheaf of topological rings.
overrides.ValuationSpectrum.isSheafOfTopologicalRi: Wedhorn’s representable condition `IsSheafOfTopologicalRings A` is equivalent to separation, gluing and the topological-embedding condition for the all-open structure presheaf, namely `IsLimitSheaf A`.
overrides.ValuationSpectrum.IsSheafyFor: Let `A⁺` be a ring of integral elements of the complete Tate ring `A`. Then `IsSheafyFor A A⁺` means that the all-open structure presheaf on `Spa(A,A⁺)` satisfies `IsLimitSheaf`.
overrides.ValuationSpectrum.IsSheafyComplete: A complete Tate ring `A` satisfies `IsSheafyComplete` if `IsSheafyFor A A⁺` holds for every ring of integral elements `A⁺`.
overrides.ValuationSpectrum.IsSheafyTateRing: A Tate ring `A` satisfies `IsSheafyTateRing` if, for every pair of definition and every ring of integral elements of the resulting completion, the completed pair is sheafy. This is the choice-independent Tate-ring form of sheafiness used in the paper.
overrides.ValuationSpectrum.isSheafyFor_congr: Any two rings of integral elements in the same complete Tate ring give equivalent pair-level sheafiness conditions.
overrides.ValuationSpectrum.isSheafyFor_iff_standa: For a complete Tate ring, pair-level sheafiness for any ring of integral elements is equivalent to the plus-ring-independent standard rational-cover condition.
overrides.ValuationSpectrum.isSheafyFor_iff_isShea: For a complete Tate ring, sheafiness for one ring of integral elements is equivalent to sheafiness for every ring of integral elements.
overrides.ValuationSpectrum.isSheafyTateRing_iff_f: For any pair of definition `P`, the Tate ring `A` is sheafy if and only if the completion model determined by `P` is sheafy for every ring of integral elements.
overrides.ValuationSpectrum.isSheafyTateRing_iff_i: If `A` is complete, the Tate-ring condition `IsSheafyTateRing A` is equivalent to `IsSheafyComplete A`; completion introduces no further choice.
overrides.MvPowerSeries.IsRestricted: A formal power series is restricted if its coefficients tend to zero: every neighbourhood of zero contains all but finitely many coefficients. These are the elements of `A⟨T₁,…,Tₖ⟩`.
overrides.restrictedMvPowerSeriesSubring: `restrictedMvPowerSeriesSubring k A` is the subring of `A⦃T₁,…,Tₖ⦄` consisting of restricted series; mathematically it is `A⟨T₁,…,Tₖ⟩`.
overrides.IsStronglyNoetherian: A topological ring `A` is strongly noetherian when `A⟨T₁,…,Tₖ⟩` is noetherian for every `k ≥ 0`. For complete `A`, this is the condition appearing in Wedhorn’s definition.
overrides.FiniteJetOver.L: `L K` is the radius-one Laurent algebra `K⟨W,W⁻¹⟩`.
overrides.FiniteJetOver.JetB: `JetB K` is `𝓑 = K⟨W,Q⟩/(Q²)`, represented in Lean as the dual numbers over `K⟨W⟩`.
overrides.FiniteJetOver.JetD: `JetD K` is `𝓓 = K⟨W,W⁻¹⟩⟨Q⟩/(Q²)`, represented in Lean as the dual numbers over `K⟨W,W⁻¹⟩`.
overrides.FiniteJetOver.jetSupport: Inside `𝓒 = K⟨W,W⁻¹⟩⟨Q⟩`, this is the subring of series `∑ₙ aₙQⁿ` for which `a₀,a₁ ∈ K⟨W⟩`; no condition is imposed on `aₙ` for `n ≥ 2`. Equivalently, its elements have the form `a₀ + Qa₁ + Q²h` with `h ∈ K⟨W,W⁻¹⟩⟨Q⟩`.
overrides.FiniteJetOver.JetA: `JetA K` is the preceding subring of `𝓒`, with the norm and topology inherited from `𝓒`; it is the Lean model of the paper’s ring `A`.
overrides.FiniteJetOver.isClosed_jetSupport: The support condition defining the finite-jet algebra `𝓐` cuts out a closed subring of the complete ring `𝓒`: membership of the constant and linear `Q`-coefficients in `K⟨W⟩` is a closed condition. The immediately following instance therefore makes `𝓐` complete.
overrides.FiniteJetOver.milnorRow_exact: For every pair `(b,c) ∈ 𝓑 × 𝓒` with the same image in `𝓓`, there is a unique `a ∈ 𝓐` mapping to `(b,c)`. Hence `𝓐 ≅ 𝓑 ×_𝓓 𝓒`.
overrides.FiniteJetOver.isTateRing_JetA: With a chosen uniformizer of `K`, the finite-jet algebra `𝓐` is a Tate ring.
overrides.FiniteJetOver.isPowerBounded_JetA_iff: An element of `𝓐` is power-bounded if and only if its norm is at most one. Lean first proves `‖aⁿ‖=‖a‖ⁿ`; norm at most one bounds the powers, while norm greater than one contradicts topological boundedness after testing against a small power of the uniformizer. Thus `𝓐°` is the norm unit ball, which is the paper’s `A₀`.
overrides.FiniteJetOver.finiteJet_isDomain: The finite-jet algebra `𝓐` is an integral domain. The Laurent Gauss norm is multiplicative, hence so is the restricted Gauss norm on `𝓒`; `𝓐` is then a subring of the domain `𝓒`.
overrides.FiniteJetOver.finiteJet_not_noetherian: The finite-jet algebra `𝓐` is not noetherian. If the kernel of the two-jet map were finitely generated, comparison of the `Q²`-coefficients would make `K⟨W,W⁻¹⟩` finite over `K⟨W⟩`; this would make `W⁻¹` integral, contrary to the lowest Laurent coefficient of a monic relation.
overrides.FiniteJetOver.finiteJet_isUniform_of_dvr: If the valuation ring of `K` is a discrete valuation ring, then `𝓐` is uniform.
overrides.FiniteJetOver.finiteJet_not_stablyUnifor: If the valuation ring of `K` is a discrete valuation ring, then `𝓐` is not stably uniform.
overrides.FiniteJetOver.isSheafy_JetA: Choose a uniformizer of `K` and suppose that the unit ball of `K` is noetherian. Then the maximal pair `(𝓐,𝓐°)` satisfies the finite rational-cover condition `IsSheafy`. Lean pushes a cover and matching family to the sheafy vertices `𝓑,𝓒,𝓓`, glues over `𝓑` and `𝓒`, uses separation over `𝓓`, and pulls the result back through the localized Milnor row. The restriction map has the closed matching equalizer as its range, so a closed-range theorem makes it a topological embedding.
overrides.FiniteJetOver.isSheafy_JetA_of_dvr: If the valuation ring of `K` is a discrete valuation ring, then the maximal pair `(𝓐,𝓐°)` satisfies the finite rational-cover condition `IsSheafy`.
overrides.FiniteJetOver.finiteJet_isSheafyFor: Choose a uniformizer of `K` and suppose that the unit ball of `K` is noetherian. Then the all-open structure presheaf on `Spa(𝓐,𝓐°)` is a sheaf of topological rings.
overrides.FiniteJetOver.finiteJet_isSheafyComplete: Choose a uniformizer of `K` and suppose that the unit ball of `K` is noetherian. Then `(𝓐,A⁺)` is sheafy for every ring of integral elements `A⁺` of `𝓐`.
overrides.FiniteJetOver.finiteJet_isSheafyTateRing: Choose a uniformizer of `K` and suppose that the unit ball of `K` is noetherian. Then every completion model of `𝓐` is sheafy for every ring of integral elements.
overrides.FiniteJetOver.finiteJet_isSheafyFor_of_d: If the valuation ring of `K` is a discrete valuation ring, then the all-open structure presheaf on `Spa(𝓐,𝓐°)` is a sheaf of topological rings.
overrides.FiniteJetOver.finiteJet_isSheafyComplete: If the valuation ring of `K` is a discrete valuation ring, then `(𝓐,A⁺)` is sheafy for every ring of integral elements `A⁺` of `𝓐`.
overrides.FiniteJetOver.finiteJet_isSheafyTateRing: If the valuation ring of `K` is a discrete valuation ring, then every completion model of `𝓐` is sheafy for every ring of integral elements.
overrides.FiniteJetOver.finiteJet_structurePreshea: If the valuation ring of `K` is a discrete valuation ring and `A⁺` is any ring of integral elements of `𝓐`, then the all-open structure presheaf on `Spa(𝓐,A⁺)` is a sheaf of topological rings.
overrides.FiniteJetOver.chartEquiv: There is a ring equivalence between the rational chart `𝒪_𝓐({|W| ≤ |ϖ|})` and `K⟨X,Q⟩/(Q²)`. The forward map takes the first two `Q`-coefficients and rescales `W` to `ϖX`; the completed chart kills every element whose first two `Q`-coefficients vanish. The inverse evaluates `K⟨X⟩` at `W/ϖ` and adjoins the square-zero image of `Q`. The inverse identities use the two-jet decomposition and polynomial density. The companion continuity theorems make this a homeomorphism.
overrides.FiniteJetOver.chartEquiv_canonicalMap_W: Under the chart equivalence, the canonical generators satisfy `W ↦ ϖX` and `Q ↦ Q`, as in Proposition 4.1.
overrides.FiniteJetOver.not_isUniform_chart: The rational chart `𝒪_𝓐({|W| ≤ |ϖ|})` is not uniform.
overrides.FiniteJetOver.StrictLoc.ext_pair_injecti: For the relation ideals `I_E ⊂ T_E`, the canonical map `I_A → I_B ×_{I_D} I_C` is injective.
overrides.FiniteJetOver.StrictLoc.ideal_row_surjec: The map `I_B ⊕ I_C → I_D` is surjective with controlled lifts: there is a constant `C` such that an element `y∈I_D` has a lift from `I_C` of norm at most `C‖y‖`. Lean lifts through `d₁` over `D` and then uses the norm-preserving coefficientwise section `T_D→T_C`.
overrides.FiniteJetOver.StrictLoc.ideal_pullback_c: Every compatible pair `(x_B,x_C)∈I_B×_{I_D}I_C` has a lift `x_A∈I_A` with `‖x_A‖≤C max(‖x_B‖,‖x_C‖)` for one fixed constant `C`. Lean chooses controlled `d₁`-lifts over `B,C`, corrects their difference by a controlled `d₂`-lift over `D`, lifts that correction coefficientwise to `C`, and then uses the ambient Milnor pullback.
overrides.FiniteJetOver.StrictLoc.isClosed_IA: The relation ideal `I_A = (gT_i-f_i)_i` is closed in `T_A`.
overrides.FiniteJetOver.StrictLoc.loc_row_exact: For every rational datum, the sequence `0 → A_α → B_α ⊕ C_α → D_α → 0` is algebraically exact. For a compatible pair of quotient classes, Lean corrects the defect of chosen representatives by a lift from `I_C`, after which the ambient coefficientwise Milnor row supplies the required representative over `A`.
overrides.FiniteJetOver.StrictLoc.loc_pair_isEmbed: For every rational datum, the canonical map `A_α → B_α ×_{D_α} C_α` is a topological embedding. Lean proves a quotient-norm estimate `‖x‖≤C max(‖x_B‖,‖x_C‖)` by correcting nearly minimal representatives; this makes the map antilipschitz. Together with algebraic exactness, it identifies `A_α` with the topological fibre product.
overrides.FiniteJetOver.StrictLoc.locRhoC_surjecti: For every rational datum, the induced map `C_α → D_α` is surjective.
overrides.WeightedParity.wpWeight: For a finitely supported exponent vector `ν`, `wpWeight w ν` is the sum of `w(n)` over the nonzero indices at which `νₙ` is odd. Index zero is reserved for the variable `W` and does not contribute.
overrides.WeightedParity.WPMem: An exponent vector belongs to the weighted-parity support precisely when its exponent of `W` is at least its parity weight. For `w(n)=n`, this is the paper’s monoid `S = {(a,ν) : a ≥ ω(ν)}`.
overrides.WeightedParity.wpSupport: Inside the countable restricted Tate algebra `K⟨W,U₁,U₂,…⟩`, `wpSupport K w` consists of the series whose coefficients vanish outside the weighted-parity support monoid.
overrides.WeightedParity.WPA: `WPA K w` is the weighted-parity support subring with the norm and topology inherited from the countable restricted Tate algebra.
overrides.WeightedParity.norm_constA: The constant-series embedding `K → 𝒜` preserves the norm.
overrides.WeightedParity.idWeight: `idWeight(n)=n` is the weight used in the paper.
overrides.WeightedParity.WPAid: `WPAid K` is `WPA K idWeight`; it is the Lean model of the paper’s weighted-parity algebra `𝒜`.
overrides.WeightedParity.isTateRing_WPA: A chosen uniformizer of `K` gives `WPA K w` a topologically nilpotent unit, and hence makes it a Tate ring.
overrides.WeightedParity.weightedParity_isUniform_: If the valuation ring of `K` is a discrete valuation ring, then the weighted-parity algebra `𝒜` is uniform. Lean uses multiplicativity of the inherited countable Gauss norm to identify the power-bounded elements with the norm unit ball and then bounds that unit ball.
overrides.WeightedParity.weightedParity_isDomain: The weighted-parity algebra `𝒜` is an integral domain. It is a support subring of the countable restricted Tate algebra, whose Gauss norm is multiplicative.
overrides.WeightedParity.weightedParity_powerBound: The power-bounded elements of `𝒜` are exactly its norm unit ball. This is the ring denoted `𝒜₀` in the paper.
overrides.WeightedParity.weightedParity_not_noethe: The weighted-parity algebra `𝒜` is not noetherian. Coefficient extraction gives maps that kill `Z₁,…,Z_m` but not `Z_{m+1}`, so the ideal generated by all `Z_n=U_n²` is not finitely generated.
overrides.WeightedParity.weightedParity_isSheafyCo: If the valuation ring of `K` is a discrete valuation ring, then `(𝒜,A⁺)` is sheafy for every ring of integral elements `A⁺`. Lean moves a finite rational cover into one affinoid head, glues each tail coefficient there, and uses the head restriction embedding to show the glued coefficients tend to zero. The global restriction range is the closed matching equalizer, so the Tate closed-range theorem supplies the topological embedding. Generic comparison theorems then pass from rational covers to all opens and remove the choice of `A⁺`.
overrides.WeightedParity.wp_structurePresheaf_isSh: For any valid ring of integral elements `A⁺`, the all-open structure presheaf on `Spa(𝒜,A⁺)` is a sheaf. This is the direct all-open form of the weighted-parity sheaf theorem.
overrides.WeightedParity.chartDatum: This is the rational datum `(W;ϖ)` on `𝒜`, defining the chart `{|W| ≤ |ϖ|}`.
overrides.WeightedParity.chartDatum_isRational: The datum `(W;ϖ)` satisfies the unit-ideal condition required of a rational localisation datum.
overrides.WeightedParity.weightedParity_chart_isDo: The section ring on `{|W| ≤ |ϖ|}` is an integral domain. Lean identifies its head quotient with `K⟨X⟩`, observes that the twist `ϖX` is regular, embeds the resulting `c₀` tail algebra into formal multivariable power series, and transports the domain property through the coefficientwise localization equivalence.
overrides.WeightedParity.weightedParity_chart_not_: The section ring on `{|W| ≤ |ϖ|}` is not uniform. Lean constructs power-bounded elements `T_n` with `‖T_n²‖=1` but `‖T_n‖=|ϖ|^{-n}`; their norms are unbounded. The contradiction is transported through the bicontinuous coefficientwise localization equivalence.
overrides.WeightedParity.weightedParity_not_stably: If the valuation ring of `K` is a discrete valuation ring, then `𝒜` is not stably uniform.
